_comment: Hand-curated Motif records (DATA_MODEL.md §2). A Motif itself carries no links; every instance (this motif shows up in that story/character/verse) is a Connection with fromType:'motif', toType:'story'|'character'|'verse', relationship:'instance of' — see curation/connections.json. Chosen only where the current content actually has 2+ genuine recurrences; not force-fit onto single occurrences.

motifs.name: Meeting a spouse at a well
motifs.description: A future wife is found at a well, in a foreign land, through an act of hospitality or defense — Isaac's, Jacob's, and Moses's wives are all met exactly this way.

motifs.name: The younger son is chosen
motifs.description: God repeatedly bypasses the culturally expected right of the firstborn: Isaac over Ishmael, Jacob over Esau, Joseph exalted above his ten older brothers.

motifs.name: "I am with you"
motifs.description: At a moment of fear or a fresh commission, God speaks the same reassurance — his presence, not a removal of the danger, is the answer given.

motifs.name: The deceiver deceived
motifs.description: Jacob takes his brother's blessing in disguise, using animal skins to fool his father's touch. He is deceived in turn by Laban, married to the wrong sister in the dark. His own sons then deceive him with an animal's blood on his favorite son's coat.

motifs.name: A child's life threatened, and delivered
motifs.description: A child's death seems certain — by the knife, by thirst in the wilderness, by royal decree — and God provides a way through at the last possible moment.

motifs.name: Famine drives them to a foreign land
motifs.description: Famine in the promised land sends God's people to sojourn among foreigners — and, generations later, home again.

motifs.name: Standing in the gap for others
motifs.description: Someone pleads with God on behalf of people who have no claim on mercy of their own — Abraham bargaining for Sodom, Moses offering himself in place of a people who had just betrayed him.

motifs.name: Grumbling in the wilderness
motifs.description: Complaints about food, water, or the journey bring either God’s provision or his judgment — sometimes both in the same story.

motifs.name: Presuming on what is holy
motifs.description: Approaching what God has set apart, or the role he assigned someone else, without his authorization — with immediate and severe consequence.

motifs.name: The foreign woman who chooses faith
motifs.description: A woman with no claim on Israel or its God chooses both anyway — and becomes an ancestor of David.

motifs.name: "Who am I?"
motifs.description: God calls someone, and the first thing out of their mouth is why they are the wrong person for it — the calling comes before the confidence, not after.

motifs.name: The prophet confronts the king
motifs.description: A prophet tells a compromised king the truth about his own sin to his face, with nothing to gain and everything to lose by it.

motifs.name: A prophet raises a dead child
motifs.description: A grieving mother's only son dies, and a prophet stretches himself over the boy and prays until life returns — Elijah for the widow of Zarephath's son, Elisha for the Shunammite woman's.

motifs.name: Stand still and see
motifs.description: Facing an army they cannot beat, God's people are told to stop fighting and watch him win it — almost the same words at the Red Sea and before Jehoshaphat's army centuries later.

motifs.name: Strong, then proud, then fallen
motifs.description: A king does well while he depends on God, but once he is strong his heart is lifted up, and the pride is what brings him down — a pattern the Chronicler names again and again.

motifs.name: The forgotten law rediscovered
motifs.description: A copy of God's law, long neglected, is found and read aloud to the people—who respond first with grief at how far they've drifted, then with renewed covenant and reform.

motifs.name: A hidden identity revealed to save the people
motifs.description: A Hebrew rises to power in a foreign court while concealing who they really are, then reveals their identity at exactly the moment it can save their own people from disaster.

motifs.name: Faithful defiance, then deliverance
motifs.description: Someone refuses a king's command that would violate their loyalty to God, is sentenced to die for it, and is delivered in a way that makes even the king acknowledge God publicly.

motifs.name: "Gracious and merciful, slow to anger"
motifs.description: The same description of Yahweh's character recurs almost word-for-word across centuries and very different circumstances -- first spoken to Moses, then echoed in national confession, in a call to repentance, and even in a prophet's complaint that God is too merciful for comfort.

motifs.name: Trust that outlasts understanding
motifs.description: Suffering or injustice goes unexplained, but a fuller sight of God's greatness turns the sufferer from demanding answers to worship and trust anyway.
